summary: Marten Mountain Tower near Slave Lake: staffed as of 2022, part of the 2022 Alberta Wildfire Detection Challenge, a viewpoint beside it that the district directs visitors to, and sources that agree on the 200 ft total height.

facts.design: Fire watch tower with a larger-than-usual cupola holding the fire-finder

height.total: 61 m (200 ft), per the district; the profile also says 200 feet in total
height.cupola: about 30 m (100 ft) up the tower, per the profile

access.note: Working fire tower. The district's page directs visitors by scenic drive to the adjacent lookout and does not mention public access to the tower. The profile calls it one of few road-accessible towers in the area.

visit.drive_up: Scenic drive up to the adjacent lookout, per the municipal district
visit.trail_note: Lily Lake trailhead is beside the tower and viewpoint in Lesser Slave Lake Provincial Park

resolved_conflicts.explanation: No real conflict on the total height: the district gives the observation tower as 61 m (200 ft), and the profile says 'This particular tower is 200 feet in total'. The profile puts the cupola about 30 m (100 ft) up, which the brief's 30 m may reflect; it is not treated as the full height. The story gives the total as 61 m (200 ft) and the cupola as about 30 m (100 ft).

notes_for_editor: Brief record says built 2017 (present structure), elevation 1005 m, access closed, staffed March to October, height 30 m. None of the build date, March to October, or closed status is in a source read, so no built event is set. The municipal page gives elevation 1,020 m; not used. The tower and the public viewpoint are different structures: a closed status may fit the tower only. The Lakeside Leader profile is the main source for staffing; it shows no visible publication date and is dated only by 'as of 2022'. Agency is the brief's Alberta Wildfire, supported by the 2022 trial and the Alberta-wide statement. Searches used: 2. Page reads: about 6.
